conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states that drinking boiled garlic water does not cure COVID-19, citing major health organizations, WHO debunking, and a lack of clinical evidence.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
**Conclusion:** Your view is correct. Drinking boiled garlic water does **not** cure COVID-19. 

### Evidence Behind This View:

1. **Lack of Clinical Proof:** Major health organizations and scientific reviews report that there is no clinical evidence from human trials showing that garlic or garlic water can prevent, treat, or cure COVID-19 (https://biologyinsights.com/does-garlic-help-prevent-or-treat-covid-19/).
2. **Debunked Fake Claims:** Fact-checking outlets and global health authorities, including the World Health Organization (WHO), have explicitly debunked viral social media posts claiming that drinking a bowl of boiled garlic water cures the virus (https://www.factcheck.org/2020/02/fake-coronavirus-cures-part-2-garlic-isnt-a-cure/, https://africacheck.org/fact-checks/meta-programme-fact-checks/no-garlic-doesnt-cure-coronavirus-get-covid-19-facts-only).
3. **Degradation of Active Compounds:** Although raw garlic contains bioactive organosulfur compounds like allicin, which show general antimicrobial properties in lab settings, heat treatments like boiling significantly reduce the active allicin content (https://nutritionfacts.org/blog/fighting-cancer-and-the-common-cold-with-garlic/).

While garlic remains a healthy dietary ingredient, there is no scientific basis for using boiled garlic water as a cure for COVID-19.
